newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to expand Jewish settlements -Sharon.
newsitem.headline: Israel to expand Jewish settlements -Sharon.

text.p: Israel plans to expand existing Jewish settlements in the Golan Heights as well as the West Bank and Gaza Strip, National Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon said in an interview published on Thursday.

"The Golan Heights will contain 25,000 people within a few years. Settlements in Judea and Samaria (biblical terms for the West Bank) will be widened and expanded, including in the northern Gaza Strip," Sharon told the Yedioth Ahronoth daily newspaper.
About 15,000 Jews live in settlements on the strategic Golan Heights captured from Syria in the 1967 Middle East war.

Damascus demands the return of the heights but Sharon and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu -- part of a right-wing government formed in June -- oppose swapping occupied land for peace with the Arabs.
A Golan settler leader said construction on 600 new housing units on the Golan Heights would begin next year.

"Ten months from today the building will begin, building that could last about a year, that's my assessment...Two years from today these apartments will be populated," Yehuda Wollman told Israel Radio on Wednesday.

The future of Jewish settlements in the West Bank and Gaza is one of the most explosive issues still to be negotiated by Israel and the Palestinians, partners to peace deals signed by Netanyahu's Labour party predecessors.
